articles.headline: RBI approves record ₹2.11 lakh crore dividend transfer to central government
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) board has approved a record surplus transfer of ₹2,10,874 crore to the central government for the fiscal year 2023-24. This is more than double the amount transferred in the previous year. The windfall is expected to help the government meet its fiscal deficit targets and potentially increase capital expenditure for infrastructure projects.

articles.headline: Sensex and Nifty hit record highs following RBI dividend announcement
articles.summary: Indian equity benchmarks Sensex and Nifty 50 reached all-time high levels in intraday trade on Wednesday. The rally was primarily fueled by the RBI's announcement of a massive ₹2.11 lakh crore dividend. Banking and financial stocks led the gains, reflecting strong investor confidence in the sovereign's fiscal health and continued domestic economic momentum.

articles.headline: IndiGo Q4 net profit doubles to ₹1,895 crore on strong demand
articles.summary: InterGlobe Aviation, the operator of IndiGo, reported a 106% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to ₹1,894.8 crore for the fourth quarter ending March 31, 2024. Revenue from operations grew 26% to ₹17,825.3 crore. The airline benefitted from robust passenger traffic and improved yields, despite challenges related to grounded aircraft and supply chain issues.

articles.headline: US Federal Reserve minutes show officials cautious about timing of rate cuts
articles.summary: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting reveal that policymakers are concerned about the lack of progress in bringing inflation down to their 2% target. Officials indicated they are prepared to keep interest rates high for a longer period if necessary. The cautious stance led markets to temper expectations for immediate rate cuts in the second half of the year.

articles.headline: Government to sell 5% stake in Cochin Shipyard through offer for sale
articles.summary: The Indian government has announced plans to sell up to a 5% stake in Cochin Shipyard through an Offer for Sale (OFS). The floor price has been set at ₹1,540 per share. The sale includes a base offer of 2.5% with a green-shoe option for another 2.5%. The move is part of the government's disinvestment program to raise funds and meet fiscal targets.

articles.headline: India manufacturing PMI remains strong at 58.4 despite slight May dip
articles.summary: The HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) eased slightly to 58.4 in May from 58.8 in April, but stayed well above the 50-mark indicating expansion. Despite the marginal decline, the sector continues to see strong growth in production and new orders. High domestic and international demand signals a robust outlook for the Indian manufacturing sector.

articles.headline: Adani Power gets NCLT approval to acquire Lanco Amarkantak for ₹4,101 crore
articles.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has approved Adani Power’s bid to acquire Lanco Amarkantak Power for ₹4,101 crore. Adani Power was the successful resolution applicant for the distressed thermal power project. The acquisition is part of the Adani Group's broader strategy to expand its thermal power generation capacity and resolve stressed infrastructure assets.

articles.headline: Awfis Space Solutions IPO subscribed 2.02 times on first day of bidding
articles.summary: The initial public offering (IPO) of co-working space provider Awfis Space Solutions was subscribed 2.02 times on its opening day. The retail investor portion was subscribed 6.04 times, while non-institutional investors bid for 2.76 times their allotted shares. The company aims to raise ₹599 crore through a fresh issue and an offer for sale to fund its expansion plans.

articles.headline: GST Council to meet in June for rate rationalisation and gaming tax
articles.summary: The GST Council is expected to hold its first meeting since the general elections in late June. Key agenda items include long-pending rate rationalisation and a review of the 28% tax on online gaming. The council is also likely to discuss streamlining compliance measures and addressing tax inverted structures to support the manufacturing sector.

articles.headline: Peak power demand hits record 241 GW amid severe national heatwave
articles.summary: India's peak power demand reached an all-time high of 241 GW this week due to an intense heatwave across Northern and Western regions. The Ministry of Power has instructed all generating companies to maximize production and maintain adequate coal stocks. The surge highlights the rising pressure on the national grid and the need for increased power generation capacity.

articles.headline: SC orders transparency in Ram Temple donation management
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust to ensure transparency in managing donations. The court will decide on a SIT probe into allegations of embezzlement within two weeks, emphasizing the need for remedial steps and impartial investigation into the trust's accounts and transactions.

articles.headline: Report on Delhi building collapse flags major MCD oversight lapses
articles.summary: A probe into the building collapse in Saidulajab that killed six people revealed that unauthorized constructions and structural additions were overlooked by municipal officials. The report recommends strict disciplinary action against negligent staff and better monitoring of high-risk structures.

articles.headline: Ragging cases at Indian colleges increase 100% since 2022
articles.summary: The Union government informed Parliament that reported ragging cases in higher education institutions rose from 655 in 2022 to 1,369 in 2024. Despite existing anti-ragging measures and UGC guidelines, several states reported a sharp climb in incidents, prompting calls for stricter enforcement.

articles.headline: IIT-Guwahati student dies by suicide, investigation underway
articles.summary: A BTech student at IIT-Guwahati allegedly died by suicide on campus, the fourth such incident at the institute this year. The event sparked student protests demanding better mental health support and academic reforms. Police are currently investigating the cause and circumstances of the death.

articles.headline: Supreme Court decries police excesses during nationwide student protests
articles.summary: The Supreme Court observed that the constitutional right to peaceful protest must be protected and criticized the use of excessive force by police against demonstrators. The court indicated it may frame nationwide guidelines to ensure police accountability during public agitations.

articles.headline: Trump warns of strong action if Iran diplomatic talks fail
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that while deep talks with Iran are ongoing to avoid military escalation, the United States is prepared to take strong action if a diplomatic solution is not reached. Tensions remain high in the Gulf following drone attacks on commercial vessels and oil facilities.

articles.headline: Mahadev betting app case proceeds may touch ₹43,000 crore
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate estimated that the proceeds of crime from the Mahadev online betting scam could exceed ₹43,000 crore. The agency has attached assets worth ₹940 crore belonging to a Delhi-based businessman and identified thousands of dummy accounts used to disguise illegal transactions.

articles.headline: IndiGo flight makes emergency landing in Rajkot after smoke alert
articles.summary: An IndiGo flight from Dubai to Rajkot made an emergency landing after a smoke alert in the cargo hold. All 185 passengers were evacuated safely, and a technical inspection found no signs of fire. The incident is currently being investigated by aviation safety authorities.

articles.headline: SC issues contempt notices to 15 states over manual scavenging
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued contempt notices to 15 state chief secretaries for failing to implement the 2023 verdict aimed at eradicating manual scavenging. The court noted that deaths continue to occur in sewers despite a clear ban and ordered immediate updates on rehabilitation and compensation.

articles.headline: India's weightlifters win three medals at 2026 Commonwealth Games
articles.summary: Gyaneshwari Yadav won silver while Bindyarani Devi and Raja Muthupandi bagged bronze medals in weightlifting, taking India's total medal tally to five at the Glasgow CWG. Gyaneshwari set a national record in snatch, while Muthupandi secured his medal in a competitive men's 65kg field.

articles.headline: Anahat Singh becomes first Indian to win Junior World Squash title
articles.summary: 18-year-old Anahat Singh secured the Junior World Squash Championship title in Ontario, Canada, becoming the first Indian woman to win the crown. She defeated Egypt's Ruqayya Salem in the final, ending a decade-long wait for a non-Egyptian champion in the junior girls' category.

articles.headline: Elderly victim of digital arrest mistook real police for scammers
articles.summary: A 75-year-old Mumbai resident who lost ₹1.64 crore to fraudsters in a 'digital arrest' scam initially refused to let real police into his home, fearing they were fake. Cyber police eventually convinced him of their identity and have launched a hunt for the real perpetrators of the multi-crore fraud.

articles.headline: UK judge labels Indian Supreme Court’s workload as unsustainable
articles.summary: Lord George Leggatt, a UK Supreme Court judge, stated that the Indian Supreme Court's current workload of hearing thousands of cases annually is unsustainable compared to international standards. He recommended structural reforms to focus on constitutional and appellate jurisdiction for better justice.

articles.headline: India summons Ukrainian envoy over death of Indian seafarer
articles.summary: The Indian government summoned the Ukrainian ambassador to lodge a strong protest over the death of an Indian seafarer on a merchant vessel following an attack in Russian waters. India demanded a thorough investigation and better protection for Indian nationals working in high-risk conflict zones.

articles.headline: HC refuses to stay probe against former KPSC chairman
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court refused to stay a criminal investigation against former KPSC chairman Shivananda Jashankar over allegations of using a fake income certificate. The court questioned how a high-ranking official could claim to have a low annual income to access reservation benefits.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Congress supports FIR against protestors over Khalid poster
articles.summary: Bengaluru Congress leaders supported the police action of filing an FIR against protestors who displayed a poster of activist Umar Khalid at Freedom Park. The party stated that the protestors lacked permission for the specific display, which violated the conditions of their protest permit.

articles.headline: Eight-year-old boy dies after falling into water-filled railway pit
articles.summary: An eight-year-old boy drowned after falling into a ten-foot deep water-filled pit excavated for railway construction work in Karnataka's Raichur district. Police have registered a case against the contractors for negligence, citing a failure to fence off the hazardous construction site.

articles.headline: Bengaluru civic body launches crackdown on mosquito breeding sites
articles.summary: The Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike has intensified its drive to identify and clear mosquito breeding spots to curb the rise in dengue cases. Health officials are conducting door-to-door inspections and imposing fines on property owners who allow stagnant water to accumulate on their premises.

articles.headline: Karnataka government allocates ₹341 crore for rural water supply
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has made ₹341 crore available to ensure drinking water supply in rural areas facing drought-like conditions. The funds will be used to drill new borewells and hire private tankers to provide water to villages where traditional sources have dried up.

articles.headline: CM Siddaramaiah rules out contesting 2028 Karnataka assembly elections
articles.summary: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah stated that he will not contest the next assembly elections in 2028, citing his age and a desire to make way for a younger leadership. This announcement has sparked internal discussions within the Congress party regarding future leadership and succession planning.

articles.headline: Police launch search for absconding IPS trainee in harassment case
articles.summary: Telangana police have launched a search for trainee IPS officer Muldani Uday Krishna, who is absconding after being accused of sexually harassing a female colleague. The High Court has refused him interim protection from arrest, and multiple police teams are currently tracking his whereabouts.

articles.headline: JanaSena Party likely to demand more seats in local polls
articles.summary: Following its strong performance in the 2024 general elections, the JanaSena Party in Andhra Pradesh is expected to seek a higher share of seats in the upcoming local body elections. The party is currently in seat-sharing talks with its alliance partners, the TDP and the BJP.

articles.headline: Udhayanidhi Stalin meets imprisoned DMK MLA in Tirunelveli central prison
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu minister Udhayanidhi Stalin visited the Tirunelveli central prison to meet DMK MLA V. Markandeyan, who was arrested during a protest. Stalin criticized the state police for filing what he termed as 'false and unnecessary cases' against political representatives expressing their opinions.

articles.headline: Death toll in Sivakasi firecracker unit blast rises to three
articles.summary: The death toll from the explosion at a firecracker manufacturing unit in Sivakasi rose to three after another worker succumbed to severe burn injuries. Authorities are investigating the cause of the blast and have suspended the factory's license pending a safety audit of the facility.

articles.headline: Co-operative bank manager dies by suicide in Kerala’s Kozhikode
articles.summary: A 40-year-old manager of a primary agricultural co-operative bank allegedly died by suicide in Kerala. Colleagues cited heavy work-related stress and pressure to meet loan recovery targets. Local police have registered a case and are investigating the circumstances surrounding the death.

articles.headline: Man succumbs to rare brain fever in Kerala’s Kozhikode district
articles.summary: A 40-year-old man died of amoebic meningoencephalitis, a rare and fatal brain infection caused by free-living amoeba found in stagnant water. This marks the third such death in Kerala this year, prompting health officials to issue advisories against swimming in unchlorinated water bodies.

articles.headline: Actor Dhanush’s fan event sparks speculation of political entry
articles.summary: A large gathering of fans in Thiruvallur to celebrate actor Dhanush’s birthday has fueled rumors about his potential entry into Tamil Nadu politics. While the actor has not officially confirmed any political ambitions, his fan associations have been increasingly active in social welfare projects.

articles.headline: Bengaluru techie booked for allegedly molesting a Dutch national
articles.summary: A 26-year-old software engineer in Bengaluru was booked for allegedly molesting a 36-year-old woman from the Netherlands. The incident reportedly took place when the woman visited his apartment for a meeting. Police are currently gathering evidence and recording statements from witnesses.

articles.headline: One operator killed as two speedboats collide in Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: A 20-year-old boat operator died and eight others were injured when two speedboats carrying tourists collided at Ramgarh Lake in Gorakhpur. Local authorities have ordered a probe into the accident and are reviewing the safety protocols for water sports at the tourist spot.

articles.headline: Kuki-Zo groups launch counter economic blockade in Manipur
articles.summary: Kuki-Zo groups in Manipur have initiated a counter economic blockade on key highways to protest against ongoing ethnic violence and restrictions. The blockade has disrupted the movement of essential goods, further complicating the humanitarian situation in the conflict-hit state.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to hear plea against release of Jagannath movie
articles.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to hear a petition challenging the release of a movie titled ‘Jagannath.’ The petitioner claims the film contains scenes that misrepresent historical facts and could potentially hurt the religious sentiments of devotees of the Jagannath Temple in Puri.

articles.headline: SC stays demolition of several buildings at Jauhar University
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stayed the demolition of several buildings at Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan’s Jauhar University in Rampur. The stay provides temporary relief to the institution as the court reviews a petition against the state government's decision to reclaim parts of the university land.

articles.headline: Bihar government to withdraw FIRs registered against NEET-UG protestors
articles.summary: The Bihar government announced it will withdraw all police cases registered against students who participated in last week's protests over the NEET-UG leak. The move comes after widespread criticism and demands from opposition parties to drop charges against student activists.

articles.headline: BJP launches nationwide outreach to counter student protest narrative
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party is launching a nationwide outreach program to address student concerns regarding exam paper leaks. The initiative aims to counter the opposition's narrative and inform the youth about the government's efforts to reform the national examination system.

articles.headline: Analysis shows 27 of 110 Radhakrishnan panel suggestions unimplemented
articles.summary: An analysis revealed that nearly a quarter of the suggestions made by the Radhakrishnan panel to reform national entrance exams remain unimplemented. The panel had recommended significant structural changes to the National Testing Agency to prevent paper leaks and ensure fair testing.

articles.headline: HC gives Sonia and Rahul Gandhi additional time for ED reply
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court granted Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi three additional weeks to respond to the Enforcement Directorate in the National Herald money laundering case. The court's decision follows a request from their counsel for more time to review the documents and legal charges.

articles.headline: NIA court acquits six Pakistani fishermen in 2019 heroin case
articles.summary: A special NIA court acquitted six Pakistani fishermen accused of involvement in a 2019 heroin smuggling case. The court stated that the prosecution failed to provide sufficient evidence to link the men to the drugs recovered, though they remain convicted for illegal entry into Indian waters.

articles.headline: Centre may pause pulse stock sales amid rising El Nino risks
articles.summary: The Indian government is considering a pause in the sale of pulse stocks from its buffer to ensure domestic availability. The move aims to control food inflation and prepare for potential production shortfalls due to adverse weather conditions linked to the El Nino phenomenon.

articles.headline: HC likely to order takedown of ‘Kala Hiran’ movie teaser
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court indicated it would likely order the removal of the teaser for the film ‘Kala Hiran.’ The court noted that the teaser's content could prejudice actor Salman Khan’s ongoing legal cases related to the 1998 blackbuck poaching incident, which remains sub-judice.

articles.headline: Ranchi teacher delivers stillborn after maternity leave bribe denial
articles.summary: A government school teacher in Ranchi delivered a stillborn baby after her application for maternity leave was allegedly denied because she refused to pay a bribe. District authorities have launched an investigation into the allegations against the block education officer involved.

articles.headline: Twenty rebel TMC MPs set to join NDA parliamentary panel
articles.summary: Twenty rebel Members of Parliament from the Trinamool Congress are reportedly set to join a parliamentary panel allied with the NDA. The move follows months of internal friction within the TMC and could lead to their formal recognition as a separate group or merger with the ruling alliance.

articles.headline: Gujarat Ayurved University orders high-level probe into exam paper leak
articles.summary: Gujarat Ayurved University has ordered a high-level inquiry after third-year BAMS examination question papers were allegedly leaked on social media. The university has canceled the affected examinations and scheduled re-tests to maintain the academic integrity of the degree program.

articles.headline: Health experts emphasize immediate treatment for all Hepatitis B cases
articles.summary: In a special feature, health experts highlighted that India accounts for 15% of global Hepatitis B cases. They emphasized the need for a 'Treat All' approach, urging the government to make screening and antiviral medications more accessible to reduce liver disease and transmission rates.

articles.headline: Indians account for nearly 60% of Canada’s total PR decline
articles.summary: Data from the Canadian government shows that the number of Indians receiving permanent residency in Canada has declined by nearly 60%. While Indians still make up the largest group of new residents, higher rejection rates and stricter immigration rules have significantly impacted overall numbers.

articles.headline: Indian-origin astronaut Anil Menon to perform his maiden spacewalk
articles.summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon is scheduled to perform his first spacewalk next week at the International Space Station. He will be part of a team installing a new communications antenna and upgrading solar arrays, marking a significant milestone in his career as a space professional.

articles.headline: Indian-origin woman shot dead in Canada; local suspect at large
articles.summary: A 25-year-old woman of Indian descent was shot dead in Toronto, Canada. Local police have identified a suspect but are yet to make an arrest. The motive for the killing is currently unknown, and authorities are appealing to the public for information to help locate the perpetrator.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strike in Russia kills five people, including a child
articles.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on a residential building in Russia’s Kursk region killed five people, including a young child. The incident is part of an escalation in cross-border drone attacks as both nations target energy infrastructure and military sites along their shared boundary.

articles.headline: Three killed in shooting at Seattle food festival; suspect arrested
articles.summary: A gunman opened fire at a crowded food festival in Seattle, killing three people and injuring four others. Police quickly apprehended the suspect at the scene. The incident has renewed debates over public safety and gun control measures at large-scale community events in the United States.

articles.headline: Tata Sons’ new business ventures report increased losses in FY26
articles.summary: Tata Sons’ 16 privately held new business ventures, including digital and semiconductor manufacturing, reported a combined loss of over ₹27,000 crore. While revenues have grown, high initial investment costs and gestation periods for these ventures continue to weigh on the group's overall profitability.

articles.headline: Number of billionaires in India grows 4-fold in five years
articles.summary: Government data revealed that the number of individuals in India reporting a gross total income of over ₹100 crore has grown nearly four times to 576 in the last five years. This reflects a significant concentration of wealth among high-net-worth individuals amidst broader economic shifts.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rejects Sun Pharma plea in Bevatas trademark row
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a plea by Sun Pharmaceuticals against Intas Pharmaceuticals regarding the trademark ‘Bevatas.’ The court ruled there was no likelihood of consumer confusion between the products, as they are prescription drugs used by specialized medical professionals.

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders CBI probe into financial irregularities at Parsvnath Developers
articles.summary: The Supreme Court handed over the investigation into alleged financial irregularities by Parsvnath Developers to the CBI and the Economic Offences Wing. The court cited the need for a high-level probe into complaints from thousands of homebuyers who have not received their promised properties.

articles.headline: Indian paddlers make solid start at 2026 Commonwealth Games
articles.summary: The Indian table tennis teams secured convincing 3-0 victories over Zimbabwe and Wales in their opening group matches at the 2026 CWG. Both the men's and women's squads dominated their opponents, showcasing India's depth and strength in the sport on the opening day of competition.

articles.headline: Andrea Pirlo out of running for Italy national team coach job
articles.summary: Former Italian legend Andrea Pirlo is no longer in contention for the Italy national team coaching position. Reports indicate that a conflict of interest involving his personal sponsorships and the national team's apparel deal led to his exclusion from the final shortlist of candidates.

articles.headline: Murali Sreeshankar and Shirse enter athletic finals at Commonwealth Games
articles.summary: Long jumper Murali Sreeshankar and hurdler Murali Shirse secured their spots in the finals of their respective events at the Glasgow CWG. Sreeshankar qualified with a strong jump of 8.01m, while Shirse impressed in the 110m hurdles heats to advance as one of the fastest qualifiers.

articles.headline: Swimmer Sajan Prakash qualifies for 200m butterfly final at CWG
articles.summary: Two-time Olympian Sajan Prakash qualified for the 200m butterfly final at the Glasgow CWG after finishing sixth fastest overall in the heats. Prakash clocked a time of 1:58.59, marking a return to form for the veteran swimmer as he aims for a podium finish in his signature event.

articles.headline: Indian sitar player Rishab Sharma to perform at CWG closing ceremony
articles.summary: Indian sitar player Rishab Rikhiram Sharma is set to perform at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games. He will join international stars in a 20-minute cultural performance that will showcase a blend of traditional Indian music and contemporary global sounds.

articles.headline: PSBs Rush to Sell Stressed Loans Ahead of Tougher RBI Rules
articles.summary: Indian public sector banks are accelerating the sale of legacy bad loans to asset reconstruction companies, offering ₹50,000 crore of stressed assets in Q1. The move precedes the RBI’s expected credit loss (ECL) framework, effective April 2027, which will require banks to recognize potential losses earlier. Private lenders put up an additional ₹8,000 crore for sale in the same period.

articles.headline: Losses Double at Tata Sons’ Private Growth Ventures in FY26
articles.summary: Aggregate losses across 16 privately-held Tata Sons businesses nearly doubled to ₹27,854 crore in FY26, led by significant setbacks in aviation, digital, and electronics. Air India and Air India Express reported a combined net loss of ₹22,238 crore. Chairman N. Chandrasekaran cited airspace closures, high fuel prices, and aircraft delivery delays as major factors affecting performance.

articles.headline: Technology Explored to Secure Indian Exams Against Widespread Paper Leaks
articles.summary: Following high-profile leaks in exams like NEET-UG, India is exploring technological solutions such as encrypted digital delivery, biometric authentication, and AI surveillance. While technology can reduce impersonation and leaks, experts warn that insider collusion remains a vulnerability. The Centre has also proposed a Bill with prison terms up to 10 years to deter organized exam fraud.

articles.headline: China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies Valuation Hits Half a Trillion Dollars
articles.summary: Shares of Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies surged 470% upon listing on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, valuing the firm at nearly half a trillion dollars. The company holds an 8% global market share. Meanwhile, India is pursuing its own Semiconductor Mission with a ₹1.3 trillion outlay to develop an end-to-end value chain, though it currently trails global leaders.

articles.headline: Gen Z Cohort Projected to Comprise One Quarter of India’s Population
articles.summary: India is currently home to approximately 368 million members of Generation Z (born 1997-2011), representing one in four Indians. Projected population figures for 2026 suggest that Gen Z will be the largest cohort at 25.4%, followed by Millennials at 22.5% and Gen Alpha at 21.7%. This demographic shift highlights the increasing influence of younger generations on India's economy and culture.

articles.headline: New US Tariffs Pose Risk to Indian Export Growth and Competitiveness
articles.summary: The US has imposed 10% tariffs on 60 countries, including India, following forced-labor probes. While India holds a marginal edge over rivals facing 12.5% duties, its textile industry faces a relative loss of competitiveness due to a lack of quota exemptions. A separate US probe into manufacturing excess capacity could stack an additional 10-12.5% tariff on Indian goods in the near future.

articles.headline: Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026 Features Leaner Event and Medal Schedule
articles.summary: The upcoming 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow will feature 215 medal events across 10 sports. This represents a significant reduction from the typical schedule of approximately 280 medal events across 20 sports, signaling a leaner approach to the international multi-sport competition.

articles.headline: India Home to Seventy Percent of the Global Wild Tiger Population
articles.summary: As International Tiger Day approaches, data confirms that India hosts nearly 70% of the world's wild tiger population. There are approximately 3,700 wild tigers living in India out of a global total of roughly 5,574, according to the Global Tiger Forum.

articles.headline: India Tightens Surveillance After Interpol Alert on Fake Weight-Loss Drugs
articles.summary: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) has issued a nationwide alert following an Interpol warning about counterfeit batches of the weight-loss drug semaglutide. Originating from Austria, the alert highlights the risks of falsified pharmacological substances. Indian regulators have directed state authorities to tighten supply chain monitoring and conduct vigilant checks.

articles.headline: Govt Moots ₹10 Crore Fine for Exam Leaks in New Bill
articles.summary: The government tabled the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, proposing a fine of up to ₹10 crore and prison terms of 7-10 years for organized exam malpractice. The bill expands coverage to state-level exams and allows for the attachment of properties of institutions involved in fraud. Special fast-track courts will be designated to try these offences.

articles.headline: Wockhardt’s Zaynich Becomes First Indian-Developed Drug to Secure USFDA Approval
articles.summary: Wockhardt has received USFDA approval for Zaynich, an intravenous antibiotic combination for complicated urinary tract infections. This marks the first original chemical molecule discovered and developed entirely by an Indian company to reach approval. The drug targets multi-drug-resistant bacteria, addressing a critical gap in global hospital-based antibiotic treatments.

articles.headline: SBI Research Projects RBI Forex Window Could Draw Eighty-Five Billion Dollars
articles.summary: SBI Research estimates that the Reserve Bank of India’s special forex window could attract up to $85 billion in foreign currency inflows by the time it closes. Foreign currency non-resident (bank) deposits alone reached $26-28 billion by July 23. The surge in deposits is expected to push India's balance of payments into a surplus of over $50 billion for FY27.

articles.headline: Govt Mulls AI Platform to Align Education with Industry Skill Demand
articles.summary: The government plans to develop an AI-powered Labour Market Information System (LMIS) to forecast job opportunities and identify future skill gaps. By integrating databases from the PLFS, EPFO, and higher education, the platform aims to help educational institutions align their programs with real-time industry needs and assist employers in identifying qualified candidates efficiently.

articles.headline: Kharif Crop Sowing Area Down by 3.9 Million Hectares Year-on-Year
articles.summary: Agriculture ministry data shows that kharif sowing reached 78.7 million hectares as of July 24, down from 82.6 million hectares last year. Acreage for paddy, pulses, and oilseeds remains lower than previous levels, though the gap has narrowed with improved monsoon rainfall. States like Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh reported lagging sowings, while Bihar and Uttar Pradesh saw higher acreage.

articles.headline: India Rejects Corporate Protests to Enforce Crackdown on Energy Drink Labels
articles.summary: India has ordered manufacturers to stop describing high-caffeine beverages as 'energy drinks,' maintaining its regulatory stance despite industry opposition. The government aims to regulate a market projected to reach $1.6 billion by 2028. Companies fear the move will damage brand identities built around instant-energy claims and disrupt established sales models.

articles.headline: Engineering Exports Surge 21% in June Driven by Strong Chinese Demand
articles.summary: India’s engineering goods exports rose to $11.48 billion in June, a 21% year-on-year increase. Shipments to China saw a massive 74% jump to $361.47 million. Despite ongoing shipping disruptions in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz, overall exports to the US, Germany, and Oman also contributed to the growth, with total annual exports to China reaching roughly $20 billion in FY26.

articles.headline: Delhi Transport Unions Plan Protest March Against E20 Ethanol-Blended Fuel
articles.summary: Transport bodies in Delhi have announced a protest march to Parliament on August 4 to demand the withdrawal of E20 ethanol-blended petrol. The Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters Association leads the call, citing concerns over the mandatory blending policy. The E20 policy has remained a point of contention among vehicle operators regarding engine performance and maintenance.

articles.headline: MRPL Issues Spot Tender for Crude Avoiding Red Sea and Hormuz
articles.summary: Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) has issued a spot tender for crude oil imports, specifically requesting suppliers to avoid the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz. This is the first time the refiner has included such a clause, citing disruptions caused by regional conflicts. The move highlights the impact of geopolitical tensions on India's energy supply logistics.

articles.headline: India Requires Eighty-Six Gigawatts of New Thermal Power by FY36
articles.summary: India needs to add 86,440 MW of thermal power generation capacity by 2035-36 to meet projected electricity demand. Minister of State for Power Shripad Naik informed Parliament that 63,545 MW of this capacity is already under various stages of implementation. Total thermal capacity required is estimated at 315,000 MW based on coal and lignite sources.

articles.headline: Centre Urges Rural Banks to Adopt Digital Banking for Faster Growth
articles.summary: The finance ministry has directed regional rural banks (RRBs) to prioritize digital banking and paperless services under its revised 'Viability Plan 2.0.' The push aims to reduce operating costs and improve customer acquisition through e-KYC and digital lending. This strategy signals a shift from balance-sheet repair to technology-led growth to compete with commercial banks and fintechs.

articles.headline: Quadria Capital Eyes Exits and New IPOs in Healthcare Portfolio
articles.summary: Healthcare-focused private equity firm Quadria Capital aims to return 1.5 times distributed paid-in capital from its third fund by early 2027. The firm is preparing portfolio companies Maxivision Eye Hospitals and Aragen Life Sciences for public listings. Quadria manages over $4.3 billion in assets and plans to focus future deployments on medical technology and healthcare delivery.

articles.headline: Nvidia to Invest One Billion Dollars in South Korea’s Naver
articles.summary: Shares of South Korean internet giant Naver jumped over 10% following news that Nvidia will acquire $1 billion of its shares. The investment will finance an AI data center expansion project. This deal strengthens a partnership established in June to build global AI infrastructure, targeting the growing demand for sovereign AI in the Asia-Pacific, Middle East, and Europe.

articles.headline: European SpaceX Rival Exploration Company in Talks for Three Hundred Million
articles.summary: The Exploration Company Gmbh, a European competitor to SpaceX, is reportedly in talks to raise at least $300 million, potentially valuing the firm at over $2 billion. The funding, partially from the Scaleup Europe Fund, will support the development of a reusable space capsule for cargo transport to the International Space Station and its planned successor.

articles.headline: Dreamfly Innovations to Establish Aviation Battery Manufacturing Facility in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Advanced aviation battery firm Dreamfly Innovations will invest ₹40 crore to set up a 40,000-sq. ft manufacturing facility in North Bengaluru. The plant will have an initial annual capacity of 100 MWh, scalable to 200 MWh. The facility targets the growing demand for specialized battery technologies within the aerospace sector.

articles.headline: KKR and Energy Capital Partners Agree to Seven Billion Dollar DCC Deal
articles.summary: Private equity firms KKR & Co. and Energy Capital Partners have agreed to acquire energy distributor DCC Energy Plc for more than £5.7 billion ($7.6 billion). Shareholders will receive £66.72 per share, with potential additional payments if DCC sells its tech distribution business, Nexora, for at least $800 million. The deal follows a competitive bidding process.

articles.headline: PayU Explores Credit Lines on UPI and Bank Partnerships for Growth
articles.summary: Prosus-owned PayU plans to expand its consumer-credit business by offering credit lines on the UPI network and potentially partnering with banks for RuPay credit cards. PayU’s credit division, including LazyPay, reported FY26 revenue of $204 million and turned profitable with an Ebitda of $6 million. The firm currently serves over 450,000 merchants across India.

articles.headline: Hindustan Zinc Q1 Profits Hit Record Levels on High Commodity Prices
articles.summary: Hindustan Zinc reported a 77% year-on-year surge in Q1 revenue to ₹13,747 crore, with Ebitda more than doubling to ₹8,074 crore. The record earnings were driven by high metal prices and lower production costs. However, analysts remain cautious as global zinc supply may improve and silver prices remain volatile, potentially impacting future margins.

articles.headline: Tata Consumer’s Growth Businesses Scale to Thirty-Six Percent of India Revenue
articles.summary: Tata Consumer Products' 'growth businesses,' including Tata Sampann and Soulfull, saw a 47% revenue increase in Q1, now accounting for 36% of its India business. Tata Sampann grew by 58% due to high demand for pulses and spices. While legacy tea and salt segments grew cyclically, management expects growth portfolios to maintain a 25-30% expansion rate in the medium term.

articles.headline: Fund Managers Launch Dedicated Reit and InvIT Products as Market Expands
articles.summary: India's Reit and InvIT market is seeing a surge in dedicated mutual funds and AIFs as assets under management are projected to reach ₹20 trillion by 2030. Firms like Edelweiss and Neo Group are launching products to provide retail and HNI investors diversified exposure to income-generating real estate and infrastructure assets, which were previously accessed individually.

articles.headline: Large-Cap Stocks Outperform Smids in Alpha Generation During First Half
articles.summary: An analysis shows that 52% of Nifty 50 stocks hit 52-week highs in early 2026, compared to 31% for mid-caps and 27% for small-caps. While large-caps have led recent gains, market participants believe well-selected small- and mid-cap stocks still hold long-term potential for outperformance. Domestic institutional flows remain the primary driver for broader market resilience.

articles.headline: Indian Auto Parts Makers Speed Up Product Development to Match China
articles.summary: Suppliers like Samvardhana Motherson and Varroc are investing in simulation tools and digital technology to compress vehicle development cycles. The move comes as Indian automakers Mahindra and Tata Motors look to Chinese benchmarks for faster launches. Varroc recently developed lighting solutions in 11 months, nearly half the typical time, to meet rising competitive intensity.

articles.headline: Delhi High Court Asks Centre to Clarify Rejection of Vedanta Contract
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has sought clarification from the Union government regarding its rejection of Vedanta Ltd’s 10-year extension bid for the Cambay Basin oil and gas block. Vedanta argues the rejection contradicts the 2017 policy for contract extensions. The court is examining whether the move reflects a broader policy shift away from the production-sharing regime.

articles.headline: Tourism Finance Corporation Targets Sanctions of Three Thousand Crore Rupees in FY27
articles.summary: Tourism Finance Corporation of India (TFCI) expects loan sanctions to rise to ₹3,000 crore this fiscal year, driven by a surge in domestic tourism. CFO Anoop Bali noted that demand for branded hotels is shifting to tier-II and tier-III cities and religious destinations. However, the hospitality sector faces challenges from rising project costs and supply chain disruptions.

articles.headline: Lodha Developers Plans to Raise Nine Thousand Crore Through Land Sales
articles.summary: Lodha Developers aims to raise ₹9,000 crore by selling 150 acres of land in Mumbai’s Palava to data center operators. The firm plans to develop 1GW of power shell capacity to lease to hyperscalers like Amazon Web Services. This strategy is expected to boost Lodha's annual rental income to ₹3,000 crore within six years as Mumbai emerges as a key global data center hub.

articles.headline: UltraTech Cement in Talks to Raise Five Thousand Crore via Bonds
articles.summary: India's largest cement producer, UltraTech Cement, is reportedly planning its biggest-ever rupee bond funding of ₹5,000 crore. The capital raise targets maturities between 2.5 and 5 years with coupons around 7.22-7.25%. The firm aims to tap the debt market ahead of the RBI monetary policy meeting, with funds potentially coming from mutual funds seeking AAA-rated credit.

articles.headline: Launch of AI-Native Music Artists Raises Commercial and Legal Questions
articles.summary: Eros Innovation’s launch of AI-native music artists has highlighted the commercial potential and legal complexities of AI in the music industry. Experts suggest the real value lies in rights-cleared content that respects personality and performer rights. However, the surge in AI-generated tracks on streaming platforms creates structural challenges for monetizing human-made creative works.

articles.headline: Trent Outpaces Titan and Voltas as Fastest-Growing Tata Consumer Firm
articles.summary: Trent Ltd has seen its revenue grow more than fivefold in six years, reaching ₹20,189 crore in FY26. It has outpaced established Tata peers like Titan and Voltas, driven primarily by the aggressive expansion of Zudio in the affordable fashion segment. Trent now accounts for 14.1% of the combined revenue of Tata’s four major listed consumer businesses.

articles.headline: Tata UniStore Narrows Losses Following Strategic Reset in Online Luxury
articles.summary: Tata Group's online arm UniStore, which operates Tata CLiQ, reported a 20.4% rise in revenue to ₹354.40 crore in FY26. Net losses narrowed to ₹252 crore from ₹314.32 crore a year earlier. The improvement follows an exit from low-margin electronics and a pivot toward fashion and luxury, though it still faces competition from global brands' own digital channels.

articles.headline: HCLTech Launches First Dedicated Small-Business Unit Among Large Indian IT
articles.summary: HCL Technologies has created 'Neo.AI,' a dedicated unit to provide software and data analytics for mid-market clients. This marks a shift from the industry focus on Fortune 500 companies. The unit aims to deliver 60% of IT work through internally developed AI agents. About 90 accounts have been transferred to the unit, which aims to target at least 500 more small accounts.

articles.headline: Bharti Real Estate Bets on Luxury Mall to Fill Retail Gap
articles.summary: Bharti Real Estate plans to open 'The Mall at Worldmark' in Delhi’s Aerocity by March 2028. The 3-million-sq. ft luxury destination aims to address the shortage of Grade A mall space in India. CEO S.K. Sayal noted that while global brands are eager to enter the Indian market, the lack of professionally managed, institutionally owned retail infrastructure remains a primary hurdle.

articles.headline: IndiGo Appoints Kiran Thadimarri as New CFO in Leadership Shuffle
articles.summary: IndiGo has elevated Deputy CFO Kiran Thadimarri to the Chief Financial Officer role, succeeding Gaurav Negi, who becomes an adviser to the managing director. This is the latest in several senior leadership changes since Rahul Bhatia took over as interim CEO in March. The airline is currently executing an expansion plan to reach 200 million annual passengers by 2030.

articles.headline: HUF Transfers Offer Limited Tax Benefits for Salaried Taxpayers
articles.summary: Tax experts warn that salaried individuals cannot simply route personal income through a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) to reduce tax liability. While an HUF is a separate taxable entity, clubbing provisions apply if it is funded through gifts or transfers from members without adequate consideration. Legitimately funding an HUF typically requires ancestral property or inherited assets.

articles.headline: EPF Reform Enables Employers to Redesign Flexible Retirement Benefit Plans
articles.summary: Recent reforms to the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) allow organizations to limit mandatory contributions to the statutory wage ceiling of ₹15,000. This shift provides flexibility for employers to combine EPF with market-linked Corporate NPS without increasing total compensation costs. The change aims to offer modern workforces a more balanced mix of stability and long-term wealth creation.

articles.headline: Global Corporations Resume Hiring Despite Previous Predictions of AI Displacement
articles.summary: Major companies across tech, transportation, and defense are increasing headcounts to meet growth goals and work alongside AI technologies. Alphabet and CSX have recently announced plans to hire more staff, reversing earlier cautious hiring trends. Some executives argue that the costs and limitations of AI currently necessitate more humans in junior and sales roles to capture growth.

articles.headline: Global Fuel Markets Tighten as War Disruptions Push Prices Higher
articles.summary: Fuel shortages are intensifying globally as refineries run at maximum capacity with zero system slack. Conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine have removed nearly 3 million barrels of daily exports, while refinery closures in the US and Europe have further reduced capacity. Analysts warn that even brief equipment outages could now trigger significant price spikes in diesel and gasoline.

articles.headline: China’s CXMT Soars to Most Valuable Listed Firm in Mainland Market
articles.summary: Memory-chip maker CXMT reached a market capitalization of $484 billion during its Shanghai debut, surpassing ICBC. The firm is leading China's efforts to achieve semiconductor self-reliance and has seen its revenue grow significantly due to AI-driven demand. While its tech trails US and Korean leaders, CXMT is poised to grow its global DRAM market share to 12% by next year.

articles.headline: Tablespace Technologies Prepares for Three Hundred Million Dollar India IPO
articles.summary: Managed workspace provider Tablespace Technologies Ltd is reportedly preparing to file for an initial public offering that could raise up to $350 million. The Hillhouse-backed firm is expected to submit draft papers by early August. The offering will likely include a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale by existing investors, with Axis Capital and BofA Securities advising.

articles.headline: Coal India Profit Beats Estimates Despite Rising Operational Costs
articles.summary: State-run Coal India Ltd reported a marginal increase in Q1 profit to ₹8,850 crore, surpassing analyst expectations. Higher coal demand for electricity generation during a record-hot summer helped offset a 12% increase in raw material costs, such as diesel and explosives. Revenue grew by 8% as shipments rose to meet the peak energy needs of domestic cooling appliances.

articles.headline: Individual Income Tax Filings Surge Past Forty Million Milestone
articles.summary: Income tax returns filed for assessment year 2026-27 crossed 40 million by July 26, with over 2 million returns filed in five days. The surge comes as individual taxpayers rush to meet the July 31 deadline. The IT department attributed the increase to technology-driven compliance measures, including pre-filled returns and targeted reminders via the Annual Information Statement.

articles.headline: Gujarat Unveils Shipbuilding Policy to Attract Twenty-Seven Thousand Crore Investment
articles.summary: The Gujarat government has launched its Shipbuilding and Repair Policy 2026, aiming to become India’s primary maritime manufacturing hub. The policy seeks to increase state capacity to 5 million deadweight tonnage and develop two mega shipbuilding parks. It includes fiscal incentives for marine equipment manufacturing, R&D, and skill creation to support a future-ready maritime ecosystem.

articles.headline: Radisson Hotel Group Expands India Presence with Ten New Signings
articles.summary: Radisson Hotel Group signed 10 new properties in the second week of July, spanning six brands across seven Indian states. The expansion focuses on high-barrier pilgrimage markets like Tirupati and Mathura, as well as tier-2 and tier-3 cities. The group currently has over 225 hotels in operation and development in India, utilizing asset-light franchise models for rapid scaling.

articles.headline: RBI Proposes Tighter Securitization Rules to Increase Market Transparency
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has issued draft amendments to securitization rules, proposing that notes issued by commercial banks be held and transferred only in dematerialized form. It also mandates a minimum investment requirement of ₹1 crore for every subsequent transfer. The changes, set to take effect from October, aim to keep these instruments within institutional hands.

articles.headline: India Stares at End of Era as Core Inflation Risks Rise
articles.summary: Economist Dhiraj Nim argues that India's recent low core inflation was driven by temporary factors like China's producer deflation and GST cuts. With household credit growth accelerating and global commodity prices reflating, the era of effortless disinflation may be ending. Refined core inflation could rise toward 5% by late 2026, presenting a significant challenge for policymakers.

articles.headline: Experts Call for Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Hypothyroidism
articles.summary: Medical experts argue that India must universalize cord-blood thyroid screening for newborns to prevent irreversible brain damage and intellectual disability. While high-income nations have established systems, India's screening rate remains at 3%. Cord-blood screening is highlighted as a low-cost, effective method to detect hypothyroidism before families leave health facilities.

articles.headline: Open Weight AI Models Present Global Security Risks for Biological Safety
articles.summary: V. Anantha Nageswaran warns that 'open-weight' AI models, which can be modified by anyone, lower the barrier for creating biological weapons. Unlike digital viruses, biological ones cannot be patched. He calls for a global control apparatus, similar to nuclear material oversight, to set shared limits on the release of AI models capable of assisting in pathogen design.

articles.headline: Fast Retailing’s GU Brand Positioned to Rival Shein and Zara
articles.summary: Juliana Liu analyzes how GU, the trendier stablemate of Uniqlo, could become a global fast-fashion powerhouse. By leveraging Uniqlo’s existing store network and hiring high-profile designers, GU aims for ¥1 trillion in annual revenue. The brand offers an opportunity to capture younger shoppers seeking affordable, higher-quality alternatives to ultra-fast-fashion sites like Shein.

articles.headline: India Requires Structural Overhaul to Fix Failing Research and Development Ecosystem
articles.summary: Narayan Ramachandran calls for a recalibration of India's R&D approach, moving beyond services toward true innovation. He notes that while the ANRF improves funding, bureaucratic hurdles and the lack of high-quality post-doctoral researcher stipends remain critical issues. He suggests dismantling independent CSIR structures to merge them with universities, following global models.

articles.headline: Government Authorizes Trial of Polymer Bank Notes for 10 and 20 Rupees
articles.summary: The Indian government has approved the Reserve Bank of India's proposal to conduct field trials for 10 and 20 rupee polymer currency notes. Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary informed the Lok Sabha that one billion notes of each denomination will be released. The move aims to increase the shelf life of notes and reduce printing costs, following global trends in over 60 countries.

articles.headline: Liberalization Was a Decisive Turning Point for the Indian Auto Industry
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki Chairman R.C. Bhargava stated that the 1991 reforms and subsequent de-licensing in 1993 modernized the Indian passenger vehicle market. He noted the transition from a small car dominated market to SUVs, driven by rising income levels. Bhargava emphasized that Indian manufacturing quality and policy support have turned the country into a global car export hub.

articles.headline: PUCC Validity for BS-6 Vehicles Proposed to Increase to Three Years
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has proposed extending the Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) validity for private BS-6 vehicles up to six years old from one year to three years. For vehicles aged 6 to 10 years, renewals will be required every two years, while vehicles older than 10 years must undergo testing every six months to reduce compliance burdens on owners.

articles.headline: Tata Sons Schedules First Annual General Meeting in Over 100 Years
articles.summary: Tata Sons has called its 108th AGM on August 18, marking a rare instance in its century-long history. The agenda includes extending Chairman N. Chandrasekaran's tenure as a director on the board. The meeting comes amid uncertainty regarding the quorum of participating shareholding trusts, though legal experts suggest the meeting can proceed even if only one trust representative is present.

articles.headline: Softening Crude Oil Prices Spark Recovery in Indian Stock Market
articles.summary: Equity markets rebounded as Brent crude fell 5.5% to $87.3 per barrel, easing inflation concerns. The Sensex jumped 776 points (1.02%) to close at 76,836, while the Nifty rose 229 points to 23,996. Market capitalization of BSE-listed firms rose by Rs 5 lakh crore. Relief came from reduced West Asia tensions and expected military restraint between the US and Iran.

articles.headline: IKEA India Plans to Open 30 Stores by 2030
articles.summary: Swedish furniture retailer IKEA aims to expand its footprint in India to 30 stores by 2030. CEO Patrick Anthony stated the company will focus on large, medium, and small formats to reach customers faster. New stores are planned for Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, and Pune. The brand also intends to quadruple its Indian revenue by enhancing its digital app and physical presence.

articles.headline: Dr. Reddy's Receives Thailand Approval for New Antibiotic Drug
articles.summary: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories announced that Thailand's FDA has approved Nujolins (Zoliflodacin), a first-in-class oral antibiotic for treating uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea. Thailand is the second country after the US to approve the drug. The application was led by Dr. Reddy’s in collaboration with the Global Antibiotic Research & Development Partnership (GARDP).

articles.headline: Tata Power Q1 Profit Rises 11 Percent to Rs 1,400 Crore
articles.summary: Tata Power reported an 11% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 1,400 crore for the first quarter of FY26. Total revenue grew 5.6% to Rs 19,439 crore. The company plans a capital expenditure of Rs 40,000 crore in its transmission business by 2030. It is also discussing the installation of modular nuclear reactors with NPCIL to bolster clean energy capacity.

articles.headline: Coal India Reports Flat Net Profit of Rs 8,849 Crore
articles.summary: Coal India Limited (CIL) reported a nearly flat net profit of Rs 8,849 crore for the June quarter of FY26, compared to Rs 8,787 crore in the previous year. Total income rose 8.4% to Rs 48,295 crore. While production decreased by 7% to 16.9 million tonnes, sales volume increased by 4% to 19.7 million tonnes. Rising costs, including contractual expenses, impacted overall margins.

articles.headline: Indian Data Center Capacity Projected to Reach 12GW by 2030
articles.summary: A report by Ludicage indicates that India’s data center capacity will grow from 2.2 GW in 2025 to over 12 GW by 2030. This surge is driven by increased AI adoption, large-scale cloud infrastructure investment, and a growing digital economy. AI-dedicated data center capacity alone is expected to reach 6,546 MW by 2030, positioning India alongside major Asia-Pacific markets.

articles.headline: EV Market Heats Up as New Players Gain Market Share
articles.summary: India's electric passenger vehicle market is seeing increased competition as Maruti Suzuki, VinFast, and Tesla registered significant new numbers. According to FADA data, total EV registrations rose 81.6% annually to 151,050 units in early 2026. While Tata Motors maintains a 38% market share, new entrants and expanded models from Mahindra are diversifying the segment's landscape.

articles.headline: Indian Rupee Records Biggest Single-Day Gain in Six Weeks
articles.summary: The Indian rupee appreciated by 0.70% to close at 95.89 per US dollar, its best performance in six weeks. The rally was fueled by a sharp decline in global crude oil prices and consistent foreign fund inflows. Foreign exchange dealers noted that the RBI likely intervened to rebuild reserves as the dollar index weakened and risk appetite returned to global markets.

articles.headline: SEBI Proposes Flexibility in Derivatives for Portfolio Management Services
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed allowing Portfolio Management Services (PMS) more flexibility in using exchange-traded derivatives. This move would enable PMS managers to offer long-short, market-neutral, and hedged equity strategies. Industry experts believe this will make PMS more competitive against Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and attract more investors.

articles.headline: Jupiter Green Energy IPO to Open on July 30
articles.summary: Independent power producer Jupiter Green Energy is set to launch its Rs 1,800 crore Initial Public Offering on July 30. The price band is fixed at Rs 214 to Rs 225 per equity share. The company plans to use the proceeds to repay debt and fund solar-wind hybrid projects. As of June 2026, the company had an operational renewable energy capacity of 2,409 MW.

articles.headline: US Department of Treasury Removes India from Currency Monitoring List
articles.summary: The US Treasury has excluded India from its currency monitoring list after concluding that the country did not manipulate the rupee for unfair trade advantages. While India met only one of the three statutory criteria (significant bilateral trade surplus), its net foreign exchange sales and current account deficit remained within acceptable limits. This reflects increased transparency in India's forex policies.

articles.headline: Indian States Face Rs 24 Lakh Crore Bond Repayment Burden
articles.summary: A report by Icra Research reveals that Indian states will need to repay Rs 24 lakh crore in bonds by March 31, 2026. This represents a significant portion of the total Rs 73 lakh crore outstanding stock of State Government Securities (SGS). Major repayment pressures fall on Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, and West Bengal, which account for 44% of the upcoming maturities.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Rules No GST on Transfer of GIDC Industrial Leases
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a petition by the central government, ruling that the transfer of long-term industrial lease rights by the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) is exempt from GST. The court categorized such transfers as a sale of immovable property, which is excluded under Schedule 3 of the CGST Act. This decision provides major relief to industrial units facing heavy tax demands.

articles.headline: Agricultural R&D Contributes One-Third to India’s Farming Income Growth
articles.summary: Research and development accounted for Rs 50,000 crore of the Rs 1.7 lakh crore total increase in Indian agricultural production value between 2024 and 2025. An ICAR report highlights that high-yielding seeds, mechanization, and improved germplasm significantly boosted output. While livestock production value grew by Rs 50,000 crore, fisheries emerged as one of the fastest-growing sub-sectors.

articles.headline: Number of Billionaire Taxpayers in India Quadruples Over Four Years
articles.summary: Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary reported that the number of individuals declaring a gross total income of over Rs 100 crore rose from 142 in FY22 to 576 in FY26. The government attributed this growth to progressive tax structures and inclusive economic development. Concurrently, Niti Aayog data suggests 24.82 crore people moved out of multidimensional poverty in the last decade.

articles.headline: Supreme Court States Police Brutality During Protests is Unjustified
articles.summary: A Supreme Court bench led by CJI Suryakant observed that the right to peaceful protest is a constitutional fundamental and cannot be met with excessive police force or lathi charges. The court was hearing petitions regarding alleged police excesses against students protesting over the NEET paper leak. The bench will also monitor the government-formed task force's suggestions on exam reforms.

articles.headline: One-Fourth of Indian Youth Outside Education and Employment
articles.summary: Data reveals a significant challenge for the government as 25.55% of Indian youth aged 15-24 are classified as 'Not in Education, Employment, or Training' (NEET). While male youth unemployment has improved slightly, female youth remain disproportionately affected at 39.73%. Experts suggest the lack of job-oriented education and R&D investment hinders global competitiveness.

articles.headline: Apex court mulls guidelines to regulate police conduct
articles.summary: The Supreme Court is considering framing guidelines for police conduct during large-scale protests, emphasizing the right to peaceful protest and the need for independent examination of any police excesses.

articles.headline: Police use facial recognition to identify over 2,800 on protest
articles.summary: Delhi Police used facial recognition technology to identify 2,873 individuals with criminal records present at Jantar Mantar protests, as part of an investigation into July 20 violence.

articles.headline: AAP to hold town hall over E20 petrol
articles.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party will host a national town hall on August 1 to discuss the impact of E20 petrol and chart future campaign strategies, alleging continued paper leaks in Gujarat.

articles.headline: Saket collapse: probe holds MCD responsible
articles.summary: A magisterial probe found the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) primarily responsible for the May 30 Saket building collapse due to negligence in enforcing bylaws.

articles.headline: Assam’ poll promise questioned by Cong. chief
articles.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge questioned Union Home Minister Amit Shah over Assam's recurring floods, accusing the BJP government of failing to make the State 'flood-free'.

articles.headline: ‘He was not part of bandh’: students’ families allege wrongful arrests
articles.summary: Families of students arrested during Saturday's 'Bihar bandh' allege wrongful arrests and violation of rights, with many sent to Beur Central Jail without proper information.

articles.headline: Hindutva supporter’s ‘shoot protesters’ jab triggers row
articles.summary: Hindutva ideologue T.G. Mohandas faced criticism for suggesting he would have 'shot' protesters, sparking outrage and calls for legal action against his comments.

articles.headline: Karnataka has to take nod of lower riparian States: Centre
articles.summary: The Centre informed Rajya Sabha that a 2018 SC verdict on Cauvery water dispute requires Karnataka to get consent from lower riparian States, including Tamil Nadu, to construct structures.

articles.headline: Mohammad Ali Jauhar University received interim relief
articles.summary: Mohammad Ali Jauhar University received interim relief as the Moradabad Divisional Commissioner stayed demolition orders for 38 structures on its campus until the next hearing.

articles.headline: Kerala names Ashutosh Dash as its expert on dam panel
articles.summary: Kerala nominated Ashutosh Dash, a former Chief Engineer, as its nominee on the Independent Panel of Experts for the Mullaperiyar dam, following the removal of its earlier nominee.

articles.headline: Seize financial documents from Shwetha panel: actors
articles.summary: Four actors urged the Registrar of Co-operative Societies to seize financial documents from the Shwetha Menon-led AMMA panel, citing concerns over the association's funds.

articles.headline: Odisha names CM’s ex-aide in missing file probe
articles.summary: Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi handed over the investigation into missing CMO files, including a report on Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati's murder, to the Crime Branch.

articles.headline: Despite resignation, Dharmendra Pradhan remains BJP’s strongman in Odisha
articles.summary: Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as Union Education Minister has dented the BJP's image, but he remains a significant power centre in Odisha politics, with his influence likely to be crucial in upcoming polls.

articles.headline: To fix unemployment, fix the economy first
articles.summary: India's unemployment crisis requires economic reform, not just education system fixes. China's approach to growth and worker rights offers lessons for India.

articles.headline: All art, no deal
articles.summary: Donald Trump's mishandling of the Saudi nuclear deal and its linkage to the Abraham Accords has created uncertainty and could worsen regional tensions.

articles.headline: Rayalaseema: India’s new industrial hub
articles.summary: The TDP government has transformed the arid Rayalaseema region into an industrial hub through investment, infrastructure development, and ease of doing business policies.

articles.headline: Why India’s youth compete fiercely for government jobs
articles.summary: India's youth face fierce competition for government jobs due to a scarcity of quality private sector employment and a mismatch between education and available opportunities.

articles.headline: How a political term can majorly fix urban India’s water woes
articles.summary: A focused political agenda for one term can stabilize urban water services by clarifying responsibilities, managing losses, modernizing services, and redesigning tariffs and subsidies.

articles.headline: How much can realistically change within the span of a single political term?
articles.summary: India's urban water systems are fragile, losing over 30% of water. A focused agenda can improve services by clarifying responsibility, measuring losses, and modernizing customer services.

articles.headline: Hong Wang makes history on winning Fields Medal
articles.summary: Hong Wang became the third woman and first Chinese national since 1982 to win the Fields Medal for her work in symplectic geometry and solving the Kakeya conjecture.

articles.headline: CJP warns of protests over ‘promise breach’
articles.summary: The CJP warned of fresh protests if FIRs against students are not withdrawn, accusing the government of violating its assurance of no punitive action against protesters.

articles.headline: CBI counsel absent, fast-track court defers hearing in NEET case
articles.summary: The first hearing in the NEET paper leak case was postponed as the CBI counsel failed to appear, leading to criticism from the Congress over the government's handling of the crisis.

articles.headline: BJP to mark 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas
articles.summary: The BJP will launch a nationwide 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyan' to mark the 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas, organizing events and a yatra from Jalandhar to Varanasi.

articles.headline: Delhi police step up drive to take down posts on protests
articles.summary: Delhi Police is sending takedown notices to social media platforms to remove reels and posts from protests, citing continuous monitoring and flagging of offensive content.

articles.headline: Mumbai Woman says she was shot in the ear during July 20 Delhi protest
articles.summary: A woman alleged she sustained 'gunshot' injuries to her right ear during the July 20 protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, filing a complaint for cyberbullying and trolling.

articles.headline: Rahul praises man for his Preamble recital at stir
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi met youth Mohammad Irfan, who recited the Preamble during a protest, praising his outlook as reflecting India's youth strength and promise.

articles.headline: Will not take part in U.S.-backed talks: Venezuela’s Maria Machado
articles.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Machado stated she will not participate in U.S.-backed talks with interim President Delcy Rodriguez, citing lack of commitment.

articles.headline: U.K.’s new PM Burnham welcomes Zelenskyy as first foreign visitor
articles.summary: U.K.'s new PM Andy Burnham welcomed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as his first international visitor, reaffirming London's unwavering support for Ukraine.

articles.headline: China supports Brazil in opposing ‘external interference’: Xi tells Lula
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping told Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva that China supports Brazil in opposing 'external interference', agreeing to speed up Mercosur-China trade talks.

articles.headline: Iran says it still controls Hormuz, not involved in talks
articles.summary: Iran stated it controls the Strait of Hormuz and is not seeking to resume peace talks with the U.S., following President Trump's decision to halt bombing campaigns.

articles.headline: Syria to seek joint security agreement with Israel: al-Sharaa
articles.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa indicated Syria seeks a security agreement with Israel that doesn't compromise its rights to the Golan Heights, while avoiding external interference.

articles.summary: The government revealed plans for several new port development projects aimed at boosting maritime trade, enhancing logistical efficiency, and creating economic corridors.

articles.summary: Public science outreach programs are successfully engaging youth in scientific exploration and innovation, fostering interest in STEM fields and inspiring future generations of scientists.

articles.summary: Master artisans displayed their intricate craftsmanship at a national expo, highlighting the beauty and skill of traditional Indian arts and crafts, preserving cultural heritage.
