articles.summary: India hosted a major international conference focused on global peace and sustainable development, bringing together leaders to deliberate on pressing challenges and cooperative solutions.

articles.headline: Young Indian Swimmers Break National Records
articles.summary: Promising young Indian swimmers achieved new national records at a competitive aquatic meet, signaling a bright future for the sport and inspiring dedication among aspiring athletes.

articles.headline: Monday Brews On One Cup of Joy For Markets
articles.summary: Indian stock indices surged on Monday as crude oil prices fell below $90 per barrel. The BSE Sensex rose 776 points (1.02%) to close at 76,835, while the NSE Nifty gained 228.50 points to end at 23,995.9. The recovery was driven by easing inflation concerns and improved global sentiments as oil prices retreated following a temporary de-escalation in Middle East tensions.

articles.headline: NPCI Gets Sole Proposal from Hindalco for Small Reactors
articles.summary: The Nuclear Power Corporation of India (NPCIL) has received a single proposal from Hindalco Industries to set up captive small modular reactors (SMRs). The project aims to provide 220MW of clean electricity for Hindalco's manufacturing operations. This follows the government's invitation for private sector participation in the nuclear energy space to boost carbon-neutral industrial power.

articles.headline: GST Panel to Examine Pitch on Group ITC Transfer
articles.summary: A GST Council committee will evaluate a proposal allowing businesses to transfer unutilized Input Tax Credit (ITC) between distinct legal entities under the same ownership or group. The move aims to improve cash flow for conglomerates by preventing credit blockage in one unit while another pays tax in cash. The findings will be presented at the next GST Council meeting.

articles.headline: Poor Rains Push Farmers toward Low-water Crops
articles.summary: Erratic and below-normal rainfall during the current kharif season has forced Indian farmers to shift from water-intensive crops like paddy and soyabean to hardier varieties. Data shows a significant increase in the sowing of sunflower, maize, and pulses. Sunflower acreage jumped 61.6%, while crops like jute and mesta saw sharp declines due to the lack of adequate moisture.

articles.headline: Standoff Ends, LS to Debate Exam Bill Today
articles.summary: Parliamentary deadlock ended as the Opposition agreed to participate in a debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill. While the government rejected the demand for a separate statement from the Home Minister, the bill seeks to introduce stringent penalties, including up to 10 years in jail and fines of Rs 1 crore, to curb malpractices in competitive exams.

articles.headline: Gold Rebounds as Crude Eases
articles.summary: Gold prices in India rose 0.5% to Rs 1,43,784 per 10 grams on Monday, tracking global trends. The uptick came as crude oil prices fell over 1% to $89 per barrel, easing immediate inflationary pressures. Investors turned back to bullion as a safe-haven asset amid mixed signals from the US Federal Reserve regarding future interest rate cuts and persistent geopolitical uncertainties.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank Fines and Warns CEO, Others Over May-Dec Issue
articles.summary: HDFC Bank has imposed a fine of Rs 1 lakh each on its MD & CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan and other top executives following an internal review of the bank's business practices. The disciplinary action relates to 'business overreach' involving the garnering of deposits from a state development corporation between 2017-21. The move follows recommendations from a committee of independent directors.

articles.headline: Govt Orders Takedown of Anti-PM Posts
articles.summary: The Indian government has issued notices to social media platforms to remove hundreds of posts containing 'objectionable and inflammatory' content targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Ministry of Electronics and IT cited violations of the IT Act, stating the content could incite violence or disturb public order. The move is linked to recent protests regarding the NEET exam controversy.

articles.headline: Tata Power Picks Odisha for ₹6,675-cr Solar Ingot Plant
articles.summary: Tata Power announced plans to establish a 10 GW solar ingot-and-wafer manufacturing facility in Gopalpur, Odisha, with an investment of Rs 6,675 crore. The project will be developed in two 5-GW phases, with Phase 1 expected to begin operations by January 2028. This move aligns with India's goal to achieve 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity and reduces dependence on imported solar components.

articles.headline: ₹80kcr Sops Likely to Push Foreign Flows into Oil & Gas
articles.summary: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is proposing an Rs 80,000-crore incentive package to attract foreign investment into deepwater oil and gas exploration. The government may bear up to 50% of the cost of drilling exploratory wells under the National Deepwater Exploration Mission. The initiative aims to reduce energy imports by tapping into unexplored domestic offshore basins.

articles.headline: RMZ-Colt to Invest ₹1.77 Lakh cr in AP Data Centre
articles.summary: RMZ's Asia's leading integrated alternative assets platform is partnering with Colt Data Centres to invest Rs 1.77 lakh crore at Jagannadhapuram in Visakhapatnam. The project will develop a massive 1.25 GW data centre park across 200 acres. Expected to be commissioned in five phases from 2027 to 2036, it will be one of the largest data infrastructure investments in Andhra Pradesh.

articles.headline: UAE Cos, Sovereign Funds to Boost India Investments
articles.summary: UAE-based companies and sovereign wealth funds are set to increase their investment footprint in India across sectors like food security, logistics, and infrastructure. Total investment from the UAE between 2000 and 2026 reached $25.6 billion. A new investment partnership between the UAE and India's Ministry of Investment aims to identify and fast-track high-value strategic projects.

articles.headline: Consumer Firms Set to Make You Pay More Again
articles.summary: Major consumer goods and electronics companies plan to raise prices by 4% to 8% starting August due to rising input costs and volatility in raw material prices. The price hikes will impact refrigerators, washing machines, TVs, and apparel. Firms like Arvind Fashions and Amisha Jain noted that high petroleum-linked material costs and oil prices are forcing a revision to protect margins.

articles.headline: Gulf States Under Drone Fire
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia and Jordan reported a series of drone attacks on their territories, allegedly originating from Yemen. The attacks follow the US decision to suspend its week-long air strike campaign in Yemen. While no major damage was reported, the incident has renewed tensions in the region and threatens the fragile stability of energy supply routes through the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

articles.headline: Tata Cos' Profit Zooms 5x in 6 Yrs
articles.summary: The Tata Group's aggregate net profit has tripled in market value and increased more than fivefold in six years. Key drivers include significant turnarounds in businesses like Tata Electronics, Air India, and Taj GVK Hotels. Despite a drag from Air India, the group’s combined annual profit crossed Rs 1.12 lakh crore in FY26, supported by strong performance in aviation and semiconductors.

articles.headline: RBI Steps Help Bring in $32 b in Foreign Capital
articles.summary: Incentives launched by the Reserve Bank of India have attracted $32 billion in foreign capital through FCNR(B) deposits in just 45 days. The scheme, aimed at boosting foreign exchange inflows, allows banks to offer higher interest rates on non-resident deposits without the usual regulatory caps. This influx has helped stabilize the rupee and bolstered India's foreign exchange reserves.

articles.headline: Eased Compliance On Cards to Lure Hospital Investors
articles.summary: The Indian government is preparing a major regulatory overhaul for the healthcare sector to attract more private investment. The plan includes scrapping overlapping licenses, decriminalizing minor violations, and simplifying the approval process for new hospital projects. The aim is to increase hospital bed capacity, especially in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, to meet the rising demand.

articles.headline: JC Flowers ARC in Talks to Merge into Assets Care
articles.summary: JC Flowers Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC) is in advanced discussions to merge its Indian operations into Assets Care & Reconstruction Enterprise (ACRE). The deal, backed by Ares SSG, would create one of the largest bad-loan aggregators in India. The merger is part of a consolidation trend in the ARC industry as firms seek to meet the RBI's higher minimum net owned fund requirements.

articles.headline: Krutrim Nearly Halves Workforce in Layoffs Round 2
articles.summary: Bhavish Aggarwal-led AI startup Krutrim has laid off approximately 40-50 employees, nearly half its current workforce, in its second round of restructuring this year. The layoffs primarily impacted the product and engineering teams. The move follows a shift in the company's strategic focus toward AI cloud services and a reduction in consumer-facing AI assistant development.

articles.headline: RS Allocates 7 Hrs for Exam Reforms Debate
articles.summary: The Rajya Sabha has allocated seven hours for a discussion on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. The bill aims to protect the integrity of national-level exams and prevent paper leaks. Opposition members have demanded a focused debate on recent exam irregularities, while the government maintains the bill will provide a robust legal framework for reform.

articles.headline: Omar Asks Mufti to Apologize Over Remarks on Use of Pellets
articles.summary: Former J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah has asked PDP leader Mehbooba Mufti to apologize for her recent comments justifying the use of pellet guns by security forces in Kashmir. Abdullah stated that such remarks are insensitive to the victims of pellet injuries. The exchange highlights the growing political tension in the region ahead of potential local assembly elections.

articles.headline: City Hoteliers to Meet Today over Swiggy Fees
articles.summary: The Bangalore Hotels Association will meet today to discuss rising commission fees and 'hidden charges' imposed by food delivery platform Swiggy. Hoteliers claim that high platform fees and mandatory discounts are squeezing profit margins, making operations unsustainable. The association may consider launching its own delivery platform or limiting services on Swiggy if fees are not reduced.

articles.headline: DKS, Vijay to Meet as State Flags Drought Concerns
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM D.K. Shivakumar and Tamil Nadu counterpart C. Vijay are scheduled to meet to discuss the ongoing drought situation and water sharing from the Cauvery river. With reservoir levels at critical lows in both states, the meeting aims to find a collaborative approach to manage water scarcity for drinking and irrigation purposes during the lean monsoon period.

articles.headline: Nilekani Panel To Suggest Reforms: Centre to SC
articles.summary: The Central government informed the Supreme Court that a high-level committee led by Nandan Nilekani will suggest reforms for conducting competitive examinations in India. The panel's recommendations will focus on leveraging technology to prevent cheating, improving data security, and streamlining the evaluation process. The move follows a series of controversies over national entrance tests.

articles.headline: Edu Ministry's 2025 Notes Flagged Learning-Jobs Gaps
articles.summary: A report from the Union Education Ministry reveals that approximately 73% of India's working-age population lack industry-relevant skills. The 2025 notes sent to states highlight a significant 'talent shortage' despite high literacy rates. The ministry has urged states to align vocational training and school curricula with current market demands to improve national productivity and employment.

articles.headline: Moonshot AI to Release Kimi K3 for Download
articles.summary: Beijing-based AI startup Moonshot AI is set to release its Kimi K3 model for public download. The move aims to challenge the dominance of global players like OpenAI and Google. K3 is touted to have improved reasoning capabilities and a massive context window of 2 million tokens. The release marks a significant step in China's efforts to achieve self-reliance in advanced generative AI technology.

articles.headline: Nvidia, OpenAI in Talks for $250b AI Data Centre Deal
articles.summary: Nvidia and OpenAI are reportedly in discussions for a massive $250 billion deal to build a series of large-scale AI data centres. The project, codenamed 'Stargate', would involve the deployment of millions of Nvidia's next-generation Blackwell chips. If finalized, the deal would represent the largest infrastructure investment in the history of the technology sector.

articles.headline: Kaynes Semicon Plots Massive Leap into Full Chip Value Chain
articles.summary: Kaynes Semicon has announced plans to expand its presence across the entire semiconductor value chain, from chip design to assembly and testing. The company is investing in a state-of-the-art OSAT facility in Gujarat and is seeking partnerships for a silicon wafer fab. The expansion is supported by the Indian government's Rs 76,000-crore semiconductor incentive mission.

articles.headline: AI Surveillance, Multi-session NEET can Restore Trust
articles.summary: IIT Madras Director V Kamakoti has suggested that the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) should be conducted in multiple sessions using AI-powered surveillance. This proposal aims to prevent paper leaks and restore public trust in the examination system. The use of advanced algorithms could help identify suspicious patterns in candidate behavior and ensure a fair testing environment.

articles.headline: Export Boost For eCommerce
articles.summary: The Indian government has permitted Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in inventory-based e-commerce for exports of goods manufactured in India. This move is expected to significantly boost MSME exports by allowing platforms like Amazon and Flipkart to hold stock for international shipping. Experts believe this will help India reach its target of $200 billion in e-commerce exports by 2030.

articles.headline: Indus Towers Q1 Profit Flat on Higher Input Costs
articles.summary: Passive telecom infrastructure provider Indus Towers reported a flat net profit of Rs 1,749 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. While revenue grew 4.6% to Rs 8,431.1 crore, profits were impacted by higher power and fuel costs and increased depreciation expenses. The company continues to expand its network to support the rollout of 5G services across India.

articles.headline: Specialised Electronics Warehousing Firms to Tap Demand
articles.summary: Several real estate and logistics firms are setting up specialized warehousing facilities for the electronics and semiconductor sectors in Bengaluru and Pune. These facilities provide high-precision environmental controls, including dust-free and temperature-regulated spaces required for sensitive components. The move follows increased domestic manufacturing of mobile phones and electronics.

articles.headline: Anicut Cap Takes Over B9 Founder’s Stake
articles.summary: Anicut Capital has acquired the stake of B9 Beverages' founder Ankur Jain in a deal valued at approximately Rs 1,000 crore. B9 Beverages is the parent company of the popular craft beer brand Bira 91. The acquisition comes as part of a wider restructuring and capital infusion plan to stabilize the company's finances and support its expansion into international markets.

articles.headline: Shoppers Stop Replaces Pvt Labels for Premiumisation
articles.summary: Retail major Shoppers Stop has announced plans to phase out several of its entry-level private labels in favor of premium and international brands. The strategy aims to cater to the growing demand for luxury and high-end fashion among Indian consumers. The company expects this shift to improve its margins and enhance the shopping experience across its department store chain.

articles.headline: Cola Wars to Enter the Caffeine-Free Space
articles.summary: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo are set to launch caffeine-free versions of their flagship sodas in India. The move follows growing health consciousness among consumers and a demand for evening-friendly beverages. The new variants will compete with local caffeine-free brands and are expected to be priced competitively to gain market share in the non-alcoholic beverage segment.

articles.headline: Adani Energy to Raise ₹3,500 cr via QIP
articles.summary: Adani Energy Solutions has launched a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) to raise Rs 3,500 crore, with an option to upsize the issue. The funds will be used to finance various power transmission projects and repay existing debt. The QIP saw strong interest from domestic and international institutional investors, reflecting confidence in the company's growth prospects.

articles.headline: NFO Flows Hit a 5-Year Low in June Quarter
articles.summary: Inflows into new fund offers (NFOs) by mutual funds fell to a five-year low in the June quarter. Total collections dropped 73% year-on-year to Rs 6,506 crore as market volatility and lack of major thematic launches deterred investors. However, systematic investment plan (SIP) flows remained robust, indicating continued retail participation in the equity markets despite short-term fluctuations.

articles.headline: CXMT China's Most Valuable Co After a Blockbuster Debut
articles.summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has become China's most valuable semiconductor company following its IPO on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. The company raised $8.6 billion, the largest IPO in Asia this year. CXMT is China's best hope for achieving self-sufficiency in DRAM chip production, a critical component for smartphones and servers, amid US export restrictions.

articles.headline: FIIs Raise PSU Exposure, Cut Private Bank Stakes
articles.summary: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) increased their holdings in public sector undertaking (PSU) banks during the June quarter while reducing stakes in major private lenders like HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. Analysts attribute this shift to the attractive valuations and improving asset quality of PSU banks. The trend marks a significant reversal from the previous years of private sector dominance.

articles.headline: Small Banks Turn to Higher Rates to Woo NRIs
articles.summary: Small finance banks in India have significantly increased interest rates on NRE and NRO fixed deposits to attract funds from Non-Resident Indians (NRIs). Some banks are offering up to 9.25% on long-term deposits. This move follows the RBI's decision to ease caps on NRI deposit rates to boost foreign exchange inflows and manage liquidity in the domestic banking system.

articles.headline: Gyaneshwari Adds To Silver Lining
articles.summary: Weightlifter Gyaneshwari Devi won a silver medal in the women's 49kg category at the Commonwealth Games. She lifted a total of 172kg to finish second behind Nigeria's Adijat Olarinoye. Devi's performance is her best in international competition and adds to India's growing medal tally at the games. She dedicated the victory to her coaches and family in Chhattisgarh.

articles.headline: AI Blows Up The Playbook
articles.summary: A deep-dive report explores how generative AI is transforming traditional business models and the job market. The report highlights the 'missing AI specialists' crisis and how firms are shifting from traditional IT services to AI-native solutions. It also tracks the impact of AI on various sectors, including healthcare, finance, and manufacturing, and the emerging regulatory challenges.

articles.headline: Shop-floor AI Drives Zebra's India Plans
articles.summary: Zebra Technologies is expanding its presence in India with a focus on AI-driven solutions for warehouse and shop-floor management. The company's new tools use computer vision and machine learning to optimize inventory tracking and improve worker productivity. India is one of Zebra's top 10 global markets, and the firm plans to increase its R&D investment in the country.

articles.headline: PFC Unit Forms SPV for Karnataka Transmission Project
articles.summary: PFC Consulting has incorporated a special purpose vehicle (SPV), Kushtagi Transmission, for a power transmission project in Karnataka. The project involves setting up a 765kV transmission system to facilitate the evacuation of renewable energy from solar and wind farms in the state. The SPV will be transferred to the successful bidder following a competitive bidding process.

articles.headline: Having 'Good Talks' with Tehran: Trump
articles.summary: Former US President Donald Trump stated he is having 'good talks' with Iranian officials regarding a potential new nuclear deal. Trump suggested that a breakthrough is possible if both sides are willing to compromise. However, he warned that the US will maintain its 'maximum pressure' policy until a definitive agreement is reached that addresses regional security concerns.

articles.headline: Dragon Trains its Guns on American Warship Replica
articles.summary: Satellite imagery shows that the Chinese military is using full-scale replicas of US aircraft carriers and destroyers for missile target practice in the Taklamakan Desert. The replicas are built on a sophisticated rail system that can simulate movement. Experts believe this training is intended to demonstrate China's anti-ship ballistic missile capabilities and deter US naval presence in the region.

articles.headline: CJP accuses govt of breaching promises, warns of protests
articles.summary: The Congress Janhit Party (CJP) has accused the government of failing to honor written agreements regarding the withdrawal of cases against protesters. CJP representatives warned of renewed street protests if detained individuals are not released. The party claimed police are continuing to arrest and harass protesters despite earlier assurances of amnesty and case withdrawals.

articles.headline: SC: Bail in digital arrest cases only on exceptional grounds
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated that granting bail to individuals accused of 'digital arrest' scams should only occur under extraordinary circumstances. A bench of Justices Surya Kant and J.K. Maheshwari emphasized that these scams are a severe crime against senior citizens who lose their life savings. The court noted that such crimes require a firm judicial stance to protect vulnerable victims.

articles.headline: Bihar to free 339 minors, drop cases against 694 protesters
articles.summary: The Bihar government has announced it will withdraw all FIRs and release individuals arrested during the July 25 'Bihar Bandh' protests. Out of 694 people detained, 339 are minors who will be released from custody. The decision follows a review of the incidents related to protests against the Agnipath scheme, aiming to restore normalcy and address the concerns of students and the youth.

articles.headline: 31GB of DRDO data for sale on dark web: Report
articles.summary: A report by Kerala-based cybersecurity firm Alibi Global claims that 31GB of sensitive data belonging to the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is being sold on the dark web. The data allegedly includes project documents and personal details of senior scientists. DRDO officials stated they are verifying the authenticity of the report and investigating potential breaches.

articles.headline: Tata Sons sees 22% surge in profits in FY24
articles.summary: Tata Sons reported a 22% jump in net profit to ₹31,961 crore for the fiscal year 2023-24. The growth was primarily driven by strong dividend income from its subsidiary, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS). Despite significant losses in some of its newer ventures, the holding company's core businesses remained highly profitable, allowing for a substantial dividend payout to its shareholders.

articles.headline: 101 murder accused part of July 20 Parliament march violence
articles.summary: Delhi Police reported that 101 individuals previously accused of murder were among those who participated in the violent protest march to Parliament on July 20. The investigation identified over 2,800 people involved in the clashes, which resulted in injuries to dozens of police personnel. The police used facial recognition technology and CCTV footage to identify repeat offenders.

articles.headline: Father hurls baby on naming function day following dispute
articles.summary: A man in south Bengaluru allegedly threw his 11-month-old daughter on the floor during her naming ceremony following an argument with his wife and in-laws. The infant suffered a skull fracture and is currently in critical condition at a hospital. Police have registered a case of attempted murder against the father, who reportedly fled the scene after the incident.

articles.headline: Desperate freshers promise first pay cheque for job referrals
articles.summary: Amid a tightening job market for entry-level tech roles, many fresh graduates in India are offering their first month's salary as a 'referral fee' to professionals who help them secure interviews. Experts attribute this trend to intense competition and a significant drop in campus placements. Recruiters have warned that such practices may not be ethical and could lead to exploitation.

articles.headline: HDFC board slaps ₹1L fines on MD, CFO for overreach
articles.summary: HDFC Bank’s board has imposed a fine of ₹1 lakh each on Managing Director Sashidhar Jagdishan and CFO Srinivasan Vaidyanathan for 'business overreach' in a matter related to an investment in HDFC Life. While an internal probe found no evidence of personal gain or mala fide intent, the board took the action to maintain high standards of corporate governance and internal discipline.

articles.headline: Man dies after jumping in front of train on Yellow Line
articles.summary: Metro services on Bengaluru's Yellow Line were disrupted for over two hours after a 37-year-old man jumped in front of a moving train at Huskur station. The deceased, identified as a local resident, was reportedly suffering from depression due to work-related stress. This is the third such incident in the city this year, leading to renewed calls for platform screen doors at all stations.

articles.headline: 576 individuals with ₹100cr+ income; 161 new entrants in FY25
articles.summary: Tax data revealed that 576 individuals in India reported a gross income of over ₹100 crore in the 2024-25 assessment year, marking a significant increase from previous years. The 'centi-crorepati' club saw 161 new members added this year. However, the data also shows that roughly 8.1 crore people filed returns, but a large portion of the tax burden remains concentrated among the top earners.

articles.headline: Shoe man: Man runs on bad road to catch min's eye
articles.summary: Entrepreneur Dhananjaya Bhadrakar staged a unique protest by running on an unpaved, potholed 1.5km stretch in Bengaluru's Rudrappa Layout to highlight poor road conditions. The 'Sprint for Street' initiative went viral, drawing attention to local infrastructure neglect. Bhadrakar aims to pressure the government to finish asphalt work that has been pending for over a decade.

articles.headline: Missing safety shield: Metro death revives demand for platform doors
articles.summary: Following a suicide at Huskur Metro station, activists have intensified demands for Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation (BMRCL) to install Platform Screen Doors (PSDs). BMRCL currently has no immediate plans for PSDs due to high costs and technical complexities across its 66-station network. Experts argue that such barriers are essential to prevent both accidents and deliberate suicides.

articles.headline: Parking facility at four elevated Pink Line stations
articles.summary: BMRCL has issued a request for proposal (RFP) to set up two-wheeler parking facilities at four upcoming elevated stations on the Pink Line: Tavarekere, IIM-B, Hulimavu, and Kalena Agrahara. The facilities aim to provide last-mile connectivity for commuters. BMRCL plans to charge nominal hourly rates for parking, with the contract slated to be awarded for a three-year period.

articles.headline: Speakers, klaxons deployed to speed up voter form collection
articles.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has deployed booth-level officers with megaphones and klaxons to urge residents to submit completed voter registration forms. The campaign focuses on high-rise apartments and dense neighborhoods to ensure 100% voter list accuracy. Officials hope these vocal reminders will prompt citizens who have not yet returned their updated information to do so.

articles.headline: 2 KIA runways to allow parallel departures
articles.summary: Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) is set to allow simultaneous parallel departures from both its runways starting in September. This move is expected to significantly increase the airport's hourly flight handling capacity and reduce air traffic congestion. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has granted the necessary clearances after successful trials of the new protocol.

articles.headline: Back-to-back fires damage several vehicles in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Two separate fire incidents in Bengaluru on Sunday and Monday resulted in the destruction of four buses and over 20 cars. One fire at a private bus depot in Nagawara was likely caused by a short circuit. Another blaze at a garage in Hosahalli destroyed several parked cars awaiting repairs. Fire officials reported no casualties, but the estimated property damage runs into lakhs of rupees.

articles.headline: GBA notifies new building appraisal fee structure
articles.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has introduced a revised fee structure for building plan approvals and appraisal services. The new rates, which vary by plot size and building height, are designed to streamline the revenue collection process for the municipal body. Residents and developers will now be required to pay these updated charges through an online portal for all new projects.

articles.headline: The monsoon sunburn you never saw coming
articles.summary: Dermatologists in Bengaluru are warning residents about 'monsoon sunburns' caused by high levels of UV radiation that penetrate cloud cover. Hospitals have reported an increase in cases of skin redness and irritation among individuals who neglected sunscreen during overcast days. Experts advise using broad-spectrum protection regardless of cloud density to prevent long-term skin damage.

articles.headline: Insta-game: Student falls for ₹2L profit bait, loses ₹2.01L
articles.summary: A 20-year-old student in Bengaluru lost over ₹2 lakh in an elaborate online investment scam promoted through Instagram. The victim was lured by a promise of high returns on a small initial investment and was gradually manipulated into transferring larger sums. Police have registered a case of cyber fraud and are tracking the digital trail of the bank accounts used by the scammers.

articles.headline: Fake Kumara Krupa website created to dupe customers
articles.summary: Bengaluru police have warned citizens about a fraudulent website mimicking the official Kumara Krupa Guest House. Scammers used the fake site to accept bookings and collect payments from unsuspecting tourists and government officials. The cybercrime wing has initiated a process to block the domain and is investigating the source of the fraudulent bookings.

articles.headline: Health security: Court quashes Union govt cess on paan masala
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court has struck down a central government cess on paan masala products, ruling it as unconstitutional. The levy, intended to fund health security measures, was challenged by manufacturers who argued it led to double taxation and lacked a clear legal framework. The court agreed, stating the government failed to justify the cess under current excise and tax laws.

articles.headline: 84 food safety officers to be recruited via KEA
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has approved the recruitment of 84 new food safety officers through the Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA). The move aims to strengthen the state's food surveillance and enforcement capabilities, which have been hampered by a shortage of personnel. The new recruits will be deployed across various districts to conduct regular inspections and ensure compliance.

articles.headline: Khader hints at free accident care and faster ambulances
articles.summary: Karnataka Health Minister UT Khader announced plans to provide free emergency medical care for the first 48 hours to accident victims in the state. The initiative also includes upgrading the existing ambulance fleet with GPS tracking to ensure faster response times. The government aims to reduce fatalities by ensuring immediate stabilization at both private and public hospitals.

articles.headline: Nelamangala farmer unearths 1,100-year-old hero stone
articles.summary: A farmer in Nelamangala discovered a rare 'veeragallu' or hero stone while ploughing his field. Epigraphists have dated the stone to approximately 850 AD, during the Western Ganga dynasty. The carving depicts a warrior slaying a tiger and is believed to commemorate a local hero who sacrificed his life to protect his village. The find highlights the region's rich archaeological heritage.

articles.headline: Promises of reform fall short as KPSC scandals persist
articles.summary: Despite numerous government promises to overhaul the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), recent allegations of paper leaks and recruitment irregularities continue to plague the body. Aspiring candidates have expressed frustration over delayed results and a lack of transparency. Experts suggest that only a complete structural reform and judicial oversight can restore trust in the system.

articles.headline: Govt bets on monsoon, to release Krishna water for irrigation
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has decided to release water from its reservoirs to aid irrigation for the Kharif season, despite current storage levels being below average. Officials are counting on a predicted surge in monsoon rains in the coming weeks to replenish the dams. The move is aimed at supporting farmers who are facing distress due to the delayed onset of heavy rainfall.

articles.headline: Duty-bound to protect right to peaceful protest: CJI-led bench
articles.summary: The Supreme Court, led by the Chief Justice, affirmed that the right to peaceful protest is a fundamental constitutional right. However, the court clarified that this right does not extend to acts of violence or the destruction of public property. The bench ordered a review of police conduct during recent demonstrations to ensure a balance between law enforcement and civil liberties.

articles.headline: Khajuraho airport has 0 flights despite 'I-port' status
articles.summary: Despite being designated as a high-tech international-standard facility, Khajuraho airport in Madhya Pradesh currently handles no commercial flights. Airlines have reportedly withdrawn their services due to low passenger traffic and a lack of demand from major tourism hubs. Local stakeholders have urged the government to introduce incentives for airlines to resume operations in the region.

articles.headline: LGBTQ+ people part of society, says RSS chief Bhagwat
articles.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated that the LGBTQ+ community is an integral part of Indian society and should be treated with dignity and empathy. He emphasized that traditional Indian values have always acknowledged diverse sexual orientations and gender identities. Bhagwat's comments are seen as a significant shift in the organization's public stance on social inclusion and human rights.

articles.headline: Isro releases first Nisar S-band radar dataset
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has released the first set of data from the Nisar (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) mission. The S-band radar images provide highly detailed information on earth's surface changes, including forest cover and glacier movement. The mission aims to help scientists monitor global environmental shifts and improve natural disaster management.

articles.headline: SC: Think out of box to plug exam paper leaks
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the central government to adopt 'out-of-the-box' thinking to prevent the recurring issue of exam paper leaks. The bench suggested using advanced encryption and digital-only delivery of question papers to centers. The court is hearing a series of petitions related to the NEET-UG 2024 controversy and has asked for a comprehensive plan for systemic reform.

articles.headline: Instagram-led anti-quota drive draws 4.8 million followers
articles.summary: A social media movement opposing caste-based quotas in education and jobs has gained massive traction on Instagram, amassing over 4.8 million followers. The campaign, which uses the handle '@reservationhatao', argues for a merit-based system and has sparked widespread online debate. The movement's rapid growth has prompted political leaders to call for a renewed dialogue on reservation policies.

articles.headline: 3-mth ban on moving stone from TN to other states
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has imposed a three-month ban on the export of river sand, stone, and M-sand to neighboring states. The decision follows reports of illegal mining and a shortage of construction materials within the state. The ban is expected to impact major infrastructure projects in Karnataka and Kerala that rely heavily on Tamil Nadu’s mineral resources.

articles.headline: Govt nod for 2bn polymer banknotes of ₹10 & ₹20
articles.summary: The Union government has approved the printing of 2 billion polymer banknotes in denominations of ₹10 and ₹20 on a trial basis. Polymer notes are expected to have a longer lifespan and better security features compared to traditional paper currency. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will monitor the trial's success before considering a wider rollout for higher-value denominations.

articles.headline: Rupee surges 66p on RBI remarks; Sensex up 776 pts
articles.summary: The Indian Rupee recorded a sharp surge of 66 paise against the US dollar following optimistic remarks from the RBI Governor regarding the country's economic growth prospects. This positive sentiment also fueled a rally in the stock market, with the BSE Sensex closing 776 points higher. Investors were encouraged by the central bank's commitment to maintaining a stable inflation environment.

articles.headline: Drones attack Iran’s neighbours as Tehran tests US resolve
articles.summary: A wave of drone attacks targeted military and energy installations in Saudi Arabia and Jordan, raising regional tensions. While no group claimed immediate responsibility, international observers believe the strikes were orchestrated to test US military commitments during a delicate diplomatic period. The US has vowed a strong response to any threats against its allies in the Middle East.

articles.headline: Zelensky visits Britain; PM Starmer signals more Ukraine support
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited London for high-level talks with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer. The UK pledged additional long-range missiles and air defense systems to help Ukraine counter Russian aggression. Starmer reaffirmed the 'ironclad' nature of the UK's support, while Zelensky thanked Britain for its leadership in providing advanced military technology.

articles.headline: Indian lifters sweep medals at Commonwealth Weightlifting Championships
articles.summary: India's weightlifting contingent dominated the opening day of the Commonwealth Championships, with Gyaneshwari Yadav, Muthupandi Raja, and Bindyarani Devi all securing gold medals in their respective categories. The performance reinforces India's status as a powerhouse in global weightlifting. Officials credited the success to intensive training camps and improved grassroots infrastructure.

articles.headline: Indian scientists identify protein that could stop malaria
articles.summary: Researchers from India and the UK have identified a protein called Ark1 that is essential for the malaria parasite's cell division. By blocking this protein, scientists successfully halted the parasite's life cycle in laboratory trials. This breakthrough offers a potential new target for drugs to combat drug-resistant strains of malaria, which cause hundreds of thousands of deaths annually.

articles.headline: A distant planet survived its star’s death, study finds
articles.summary: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have discovered a planet that survived the explosive death of its sun-like host star. The white dwarf system, WD 1856+534, features a Jupiter-sized planet in a tight orbit. The discovery challenges previous models of planetary destruction and provides clues about the future of our own solar system when the sun runs out of fuel.

articles.headline: Parliament Debates Tougher Law Against Exam Paper Leaks with Severe Penalties
articles.summary: Parliament is debating the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, proposing strict penalties for exam paper leaks and unfair means. Penalties include jail terms of 5 to 10 years and fines up to Rs 50 lakh, potentially reaching Rs 10 crore for organized crimes. This aims to protect student interests and institutional integrity.

articles.headline: Madras High Court Quashes TN Order Granting Jobs to Stampede Victims' Kin
articles.summary: The Madras High Court has quashed Tamil Nadu government orders that provided compassionate appointments to families of victims from the 2023 Karur stampede. The court ruled these orders unconstitutional, stating that public employment must be merit-based and adhere to existing constitutional frameworks, thus being unfair to other qualified candidates.

articles.headline: CJP Warns of Protests Over Alleged Breach of Promise on Student Detentions
articles.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is warning of renewed protests if FIRs against students involved in NEET-UG paper leak agitations are not withdrawn. The party accuses the Centre of violating an assurance of no punitive action, citing arrests and surveillance, and demands the release of detained activists.

articles.headline: Delhi Police Seeks Death Penalty for Ex-AAP Councillor Tahir Hussain in Murder Case
articles.summary: Delhi Police are seeking the death penalty for former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others convicted of murdering IB staffer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 Delhi riots. The prosecution argues the crime was part of a conspiracy and fits the 'rarest of rare' category due to the 51 injuries on the victim.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to Examine Flaws in Anti-Defection Law's Merger Exception
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will examine pleas regarding flaws in the Tenth Schedule's anti-defection law, particularly the 'merger' exception. The court noted 'enormous issues' allowing legislators to escape disqualification, potentially making a mockery of parliamentary democracy. The Centre has been asked for its response.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank Fines Top Executives, CEO Over MSRDC Funding Irregularities
articles.summary: HDFC Bank's board fined CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan, CFO Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, and Retail Assets head Arvind Vohra ₹1 lakh each and issued warning letters over irregularities in managing Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) accounts. An internal probe found a lack of controls, though no mala fide intent was established.

articles.headline: Bank of Baroda Suffers Data Breach: 1 TB of Customer and Internal Data Leaked
articles.summary: Bank of Baroda reported a cyber breach compromising an employee's email, exposing approximately 1TB of customer and internal data including bank account numbers, loan details, and Aadhaar numbers. The bank stated core banking systems were not accessed and a forensic investigation is underway.

articles.headline: One Dead, Three Missing After Falling into Yamuna River
articles.summary: One person has died and three others are feared drowned after falling into the Yamuna river near East Delhi's Geeta Colony. Search operations are ongoing for the missing individuals.

articles.headline: Renowned Japanese Mystery Author Keigo Higashino Dies at 68
articles.summary: World-renowned Japanese mystery author Keigo Higashino, celebrated for works like 'The Devotion of Suspect X,' passed away at 68 due to colon cancer. His books, translated into over 40 languages, have been adapted into numerous films and TV series globally.

articles.headline: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri Meets Chinese FM Wang Yi in Beijing
articles.summary: Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri held high-level discussions with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing. The talks focused on stabilizing bilateral relations, resolving border disputes, and maintaining peace and tranquility along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

articles.headline: Karnataka Cabinet Expansion to Be Finalized This Week, Says CM
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announced that the state cabinet expansion will be finalized this week following consultations with the party high command in New Delhi. The expansion aims to fill vacant positions and balance regional and caste representation.

articles.headline: Centre: Tamil Nadu Consent Not Required for Mekedatu Reservoir Project
articles.summary: The Union government has stated that Karnataka does not require the consent of Tamil Nadu for the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project. Minister of State for Jal Shakti cited a Supreme Court verdict, noting Karnataka is free to build the project provided mandatory water release to Tamil Nadu is ensured, subject to environmental clearances.

articles.headline: Telangana HC Orders Immediate Removal of HYDRAA Commissioner
articles.summary: The Telangana High Court has ordered the immediate removal of IPS officer AV Ranganath as the head of HYDRAA due to numerous contempt of court cases and his failure to adhere to judicial stay orders during demolition drives in Hyderabad.

articles.headline: Bihar Policeman Suspended for Firing AK-47 During Student Protest
articles.summary: A Bihar police constable has been suspended after a video showed him firing an AK-47 rifle during a student protest in Siwan. Officials called the action a grave violation of standard operating procedures.

articles.headline: Bombay HC Allows Nitin Gadkari to Sue Meta, Google Over Deepfake Videos
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court has permitted Union Minister Nitin Gadkari to file a civil suit against Meta, Google, and X Corp over alleged 'defamatory' AI-generated deepfake posts and videos related to the E20 ethanol fuel policy, which he claims have caused significant reputational damage.

articles.headline: Bangladesh Tribunal Charges Sheikh Hasina with Crimes Against Humanity
articles.summary: Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal has formally charged former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and 40 others with crimes against humanity for a lethal crackdown on a 2013 rally in Dhaka. Hasina is currently in India, having previously received a death sentence in absentia for suppressing 2024 student protests.

articles.headline: Air India Turnaround to Take a Decade, Says Tata Sons Chairman
articles.summary: Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran estimates Air India's complete transformation into a global carrier will take five to ten years. FY26 saw combined losses for Air India and its subsidiary double to ₹22,238 crore, with challenges including fuel prices and delivery delays.

articles.headline: Esha Singh Wins Gold, Manu Bhaker Takes Bronze in 25m Pistol Event
articles.summary: Indian shooter Esha Singh secured the gold medal in the women's 25m pistol event at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou, while teammate Manu Bhaker won the bronze, marking a strong performance for the Indian contingent.

articles.headline: Sachin, Ankush Advance to Quarterfinals in Commonwealth Games Boxing
articles.summary: Indian boxers Sachin Siwach and Ankush Panghal have advanced to the quarterfinals of the Commonwealth Games. Sachin won his round-of-16 match by split decision, and Ankush secured a unanimous victory, keeping India's medal hopes alive.

articles.headline: India Summons Ukraine Envoy Over Fatal Black Sea Ship Attack
articles.summary: India has summoned the Ukrainian Ambassador to protest the July 18 attack on the commercial vessel 'MV Omori' in the Black Sea, which killed an Indian national. New Delhi expressed grave concern over the targeting of commercial ships and the safety of Indian nationals in conflict zones.

articles.headline: Lok Sabha Introduces Bill to Curb Exam Paper Leaks with Harsh Penalties
articles.summary: The government introduced the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill in the Lok Sabha, proposing stringent punishments including jail terms and heavy fines to curb paper leaks. Discussion is expected amid protests over recent NEET irregularities.

articles.headline: Expert Panel Discusses Education and Electoral Reforms
articles.summary: An expert panel convened to discuss potential reforms in the national education system, focusing on curriculum modernization and skill development. Simultaneously, discussions covered electoral reforms to enhance transparency and voter participation.

articles.headline: Skill Development Programs Expand as Government Prioritizes Job Creation
articles.summary: Government-backed skill development programs are expanding nationwide to offer vocational training and address labor market needs. New policy initiatives aim to accelerate job creation and enhance workforce readiness.

articles.headline: High Court Delivers Verdict on Land Dispute and Public Land Encroachment
articles.summary: The High Court has upheld a verdict in a complex land dispute case, providing clarity on property rights. In a separate intervention, the court also issued directives for swift action against public land encroachment.

articles.headline: Regional Parties Form New Alliance Ahead of General Elections
articles.summary: Several regional political parties have announced a new alliance to consolidate their electoral strength and present a united front in the upcoming general elections, aiming to reshape the political landscape.

articles.headline: New Hospitals Commissioned in Remote Areas; Expressways Planned
articles.summary: Several new hospitals and healthcare facilities have been commissioned in remote districts, improving access to medical care. Concurrently, plans for new expressways connecting remote areas were announced to boost connectivity and economic growth.
